anatomy.flutter: SafeArea(left, top, right, bottom, child) wraps `child` in Padding(spend) after MediaQuery.removePadding, short-circuiting to return `child` unwrapped when the computed EdgeInsets.spend is zero (desktop no-op); companion statics topBarHeightOf and scrollPaddingOf let a bar or scroll view pay the same insets without a literal Padding widget.
anatomy.web: styles/utilities.css now ships seven `@utility` blocks — pt-safe, pr-safe, pb-safe, pl-safe, px-safe, py-safe, p-safe — each writing the matching padding longhand from `env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)`.
anatomy.note: CLOSED on review after this audit found it. The capability was named by the contract and promised by docs/architecture/platform-parity.md while nothing under styles/ implemented it; the utilities were added and the documentation page rewritten from 'no web implementation exists' to what actually ships. Verified in the browser: all seven rules are emitted by Tailwind and resolve, and computed padding is 0px on a display reporting no inset, which is the fallback working rather than a dead class.

api.flutter: SafeArea's constructor takes four independent booleans (left, top, right, bottom, all defaulting true) so a caller can pay only some edges, e.g. SafeArea(bottom: false, child: Row(controls)) to keep a bar's own bottom edge full-bleed while still moving its top row down.
api.web: Seven utility classes rather than a widget with `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`/`minimum` parameters: `p-safe` for all four edges, `px-safe`/`py-safe` per axis, `pt-safe`/`pr-safe`/`pb-safe`/`pl-safe` per edge.
api.note: CLOSED as a gap; the remaining difference is one of shape, not of capability. Flutter's SafeArea is a widget taking four booleans and a `minimum` EdgeInsets because it has to wrap a subtree; the web reads the same four numbers straight out of `env()`, so a class per edge is the whole API and there is nothing for a component to own. The contract already classifies this `css-native` for exactly that reason.

states.flutter: SafeArea is a StatelessWidget with a single build path driven purely by MediaQueryData.padding at build time; there is no interaction state (rest/hover/focus/etc.) because it is layout plumbing, not a control.
states.web: N/A — there is no web element to have states; nothing renders.
states.note: Safe-area insetting is a layout concern, not an interactive control, on either platform in principle — but on the web side there is nothing at all to evaluate since no implementation exists, so this is recorded n/a rather than gap to avoid double-counting the same missing-implementation finding across every dimension identically.

disabled.flutter: SafeArea has no enabled/disabled concept — every edge is either paid (its bool is true and the corresponding MediaQuery inset is nonzero) or not spent at all.
disabled.web: N/A — there is no component, class, or utility on the web side, so there is nothing that could carry a disabled/enabled state to check.
disabled.note: A layout-inset helper has no disabled state on either platform; recorded n/a for the same reason as the states dimension rather than repeating the missing-implementation gap.

interaction.flutter: SafeArea has no pointer, keyboard, touch, or focus handling anywhere in safe_area.dart — it only reads MediaQuery.maybePaddingOf(context) and adjusts Padding/MediaQuery.removePadding at build time.
interaction.web: N/A — there is no rendered element on the web side at all, so there is nothing to receive pointer, keyboard, or touch input.
interaction.note: Not an interactive capability on either platform; recorded n/a rather than repeating the same missing-implementation finding a third time.

semantics.flutter: SafeArea's whole purpose is an accessibility/usability guarantee stated as a ruling in its doc comment: 'Backgrounds paint edge-to-edge; content and interactive chrome respect MediaQueryData.padding' — so interactive controls and readable content are never physically obscured by a notch, status bar, or gesture/navigation bar on a real device.
semantics.web: Padding only — no role, no announcement, no target-size claim. The insets keep content clear of the notch and the home indicator, which is a layout guarantee rather than a semantic one, on both platforms.
semantics.note: CLOSED. The live defect recorded here was that a consumer rendering inside a notched or gesture-navigated viewport had nothing to reach for; the seven utilities are that thing. Neither platform annotates the inset itself — Flutter's SafeArea emits no Semantics node either.
